x-runtime-configuration.legacy: DSI_CONVERSATION_LEGACY_ENABLED defaults to 0 to preserve Agent Hub J1 /tasks stream/abort semantics; 1 requires paused or enabled and a migrated client.
x-runtime-configuration.mode: DSI_CONVERSATION_MODE: disabled (default J1), enabled (turns/scheduler/events/lifecycle), paused (same routes, new turns rejected; history/receipts readable)
x-runtime-configuration.origin: Agent Hub /agent-api rewrites to agent-api without that prefix. Configure DSI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to the exact public frontend origin; backend URL is not the browser origin.
x-runtime-configuration.process: One agent-api instance only. On restart login cookies and execution handles are lost; old work fails/interrupts without replay. SIGTERM/SIGINT stop admission/streams/scheduler with a bounded grace period.

x-transport-rules.bff: Forward trusted login Cookie and permitted Origin, Last-Event-ID; preserve Set-Cookie, structured errors, download and streaming headers. Never use Skill Market fixed principal for conversations.
x-transport-rules.capabilitySelection: Daily Agent Loop only. Malformed or forged fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST; other profiles return 422 CAPABILITY_SELECTION_NOT_ALLOWED; missing, inaccessible, revoked, or unavailable selections return 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE with a generic message. Matching receipt retries reuse the stored snapshot without repeating external preflight. MCP tools come only from explicitly selected enabled/healthy read-only servers; an empty or omitted MCP selection never queries the provider. Catalog outages degrade only the MCP section with MCP_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE. The worker re-reads the DB snapshot and revalidates before model use; a selected resource revoked after acceptance ends with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. Process restart loses the execution identity handle and never replays a pending Turn.
x-transport-rules.legacy: Controlled legacy adapter only. QA/daily aliases: /agent and /api/agent. taskId and legacy task status retained; conversationId/turnId added. userId/sessionId ignored. Preserve clientRequestId on retries; without one, each request starts a new single-turn conversation. Nonempty legacy task context/daily category require typed input via the dedicated API; fixed demos and internal task-only services remain separate. Admission disabled returns 503 CONVERSATION_EXECUTION_DISABLED, never falls back to the old pipeline. Receipt retries may still return an existing committed turn.
x-transport-rules.retry: Same send retries retain clientRequestId and normalized input, including after timeout or 503 with an unknown commit result. acceptedEventSeq is a receipt watermark, not permission to skip unapplied events. Unknown commit retains the original execution identity; retries never rebind credentials.
x-transport-rules.stream: Client fetches snapshot separately. Use snapshot.lastEventSeq for future updates only after installing that snapshot. Recover historical failed/interrupted turn state by replaying /events from afterSeq=0 (or a proven cached projection) through the snapshot watermark; activeTurn alone is not terminal history. Preserve an applied cursor only together with its projection. Last-Event-ID overrides afterSeq and is conversation-scoped. : connected/: heartbeat are comments. Named events require event listeners or a streaming parser; x-event-schema is descriptive and does not generate that parser. No token-delta replay. RESYNC_REQUIRED discards stale cursor/preview and reloads snapshot; if historical events remain unavailable, mark historical status unknown, retain readable messages, and do not infinitely reconnect or rerun the model.
